records.supported_name_scope: Isortoq River is supported as the representative identity of the selected Baffin Island corridor by readable federal map labels throughout its connected upper, middle and lower river settings. Isortoq Lake is a distinct through-route lake component. Small headward lakes and exact reach/lake name-transition boundaries are not assigned scalar names.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected corridor lies north and northwest of the Barnes Ice Cap and is distinct from the neighboring Conn Lake and Rowley River drainages. The source maps place Isortoq River labels on the connected selected river corridor and Isortoq Lake on its elongated lower lake expansion; Isortoq Fiord supplies the broad coastal receiving context.
records.completion_scope: One complete selected mainstem feature was read against a broad original map and four overlapping original detail views. The observations cover the small-lake headward corridor, adjacent Causeway Lake connection, sharp southward middle bend, western/northern and glacier-side tributary junctions, the Limit Lake vicinity, the westward middle trunk, actual Isortoq Lake passage, lower river and fiord-head terminal. This is component/corridor correspondence, not pointwise fitting, geometry validation or source-vector acquisition.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_scope: Upper Isortoq corridor containing small connected lakes and stream links; exact headmost reach name and natural source not separately adjudicated.
naming_scope_details.terminal_limit: The generalized selected lower end belongs to the river-to-fiord setting. Its render endpoint reaches the inlet setting; no surveyed mouth, bank, tidal limit or present-day shoreline intersection is asserted.
excluded_inferences: Causeway Lake and Limit Lake labels are not used to invent exact selected lake traverses or name-transition vertices.

records.region: Baffin Island, Nunavut, Canada, north and northwest of Barnes Ice Cap through Isortoq Lake to Isortoq Fiord.

records.supported_name_scope: Murchison River is supported as the representative river-system identity for the selected connected corridor. Its small initial feeder has no readable name, and Murchison Lake is a separately named lake component. The representative identity does not rename each reach or lake.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The terminal is the Inglis Bay setting on the southeast side of Rasmussen Basin. Chantrey Inlet was regional orientation only and is not substituted for the actual terminal. Darby Lake lies south of the middle selected river and is not the through-route lake; the selected broad lake crossing is Murchison Lake. The separately described Inglis River is not adopted as an alias or substituted for the selected Murchison corridor.
records.completion_scope: One original overview and four overlapping original detail rasters were read with the complete selected line used only as an orientation aid. The reading covers the initial westward feeder, its entry into the northeast trunk, the middle eastward bend and northward approach, all of Murchison Lake, the northern channel and westward lower river, and the broad coastal branching tract through the actual terminal setting. Local simplification offsets and long display segments do not require bank-level or pointwise agreement. No material geographic connector remains uncovered.

naming_scope_details.unassigned: Initial feeder/lake name, exact formal name-transition boundaries, uniform scalar label, Korean rendering, contemporary flow/channel conditions, exact bank positions and surveyed source/mouth vertices.

It is not the western Atoyac drainage, the separate San Juan headward approach, the western Tequisistlán approach to the reservoir, or a coastal-lagoon route.
